parts:
Hi everybody,

I'm stuck again... I have 11 arrays which i analysed up to the NUSE
plots and realised that one had 1.08 median SE so i decided to remove
from the analysis (do you think this is the right decision?). I
started the analysis from the beginning with the 10 arrays and now i
get an error message everytime i do process(qn). See below:

>cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core,A20071112,EP")
>cs2 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("PC3DataSet-C4",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")
>setCdf(cs2, cdf)
>bc2 <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs2, tag="BCcoreCDF")
>csBC2 <- process(bc2,verbose=verbose)
>setCdf(csBC2,cdf)
>qn2 <- QuantileNormalization(csBC2, typesToUpdate="pm",tags="QNcore")
>csN2 <- process(qn2)
Error in list("process(qn2)" = <environment>,
"process.QuantileNormalization(qn2)" = <environment>, :

[2008-05-20 10:48:38] Exception: Failed to copy file. Temporary copy
file exists: probeData/PC3DataSet-C4,BCcoreCDF,QNcore/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/
EGF.CEL.tmp.tmp
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("Failed to copy file. Temporary copy file exists:
", tmpPathname)

tmpPathname)

overwrite, verbose = less(verbose, 10))
at copyFile(getPathname(this), pathname, overwrite = overwrite,
verbose = less(verbose, 10))

verbose = less(verbose))

less(verbose))

NULL, verbose = less(verbose))
at createFrom(this, filename = pathname, path = NULL, verbose =
less(verbose))
at normalizeQuantile.AffymetrixCelFile(df, path = path,
subsetToUpdate = subsetToUpdate, t


I also noticed that there is something wrong with the algorith
patameters/targetDistribution of QuantileNormalisation as i get a
funny sequence of numbers when i do:
> print(qn2)
QuantileNormalization:
Data set: PC3DataSet-C4
Input tags: BCcoreCDF
Output tags: BCcoreCDF,QNcore
Number of arrays: 10 (627.94MB)
Chip type: HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core,A20071112,EP
Algorithm parameters: (subsetToUpdate: NULL, typesToUpdate: chr "pm",
subsetToAvg: NULL, typesToAvg: chr "pm", .targetDistribution: atomic
[1:1082385] 2.65 2.70 2.74 2.76 2.77 ..., ..- attr(*, "identifier")=
chr "0eaa5518c2aece6a8cd6593a19951570")
Output path: probeData/PC3DataSet-C4,BCcoreCDF,QNcore/HuEx-1_0-st-v2
Is done: FALSE
RAM: 8.26MB

So just to play i did:
>qn2 <- QuantileNormalization(csBC2, typesToUpdate="pm",targetDistribution=NULL, tags="QNcore")
...but it didn't work...

Can you help???
Thanks,
Maria

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] targetDistribution: atomic...
parts:
Hi Maria.

I can't speculate as to what has happened (maybe Elizabeth or Henrik
can ...), but the error message suggests that a 'copy file' was left
over from a previous run.

I would delete all the files in:
./probeData/PC3DataSet-C4,BCcoreCDF,QNcore/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/

and rerun the final 2 steps:

qn2 <- QuantileNormalization(csBC2, typesToUpdate="pm",tags="QNcore")
csN2<- process(qn2)

Does that run?

Failing that, you could remove everything in:
./probeData/PC3DataSet-C4,BCcoreCDF/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/
... and go back a few more commands.

As to 1.08 ... if that median sticks way out from the rest, then I
would agree with your decision.

Cheers,
Mark

parts: Hi.

On Tue, May 20, 2008 at 3:08 AM, Maria Traka <maria...@bbsrc.ac.uk> wrote:
>
> Hi everybody,
>
> I'm stuck again... I have 11 arrays which i analysed up to the NUSE
> plots and realised that one had 1.08 median SE so i decided to remove
> from the analysis (do you think this is the right decision?). I
> started the analysis from the beginning with the 10 arrays and now i
> get an error message everytime i do process(qn). See below:
>
>>cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core,A20071112,EP")
>>cs2 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("PC3DataSet-C4",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")
>>setCdf(cs2, cdf)

FYI, the latter two lines are preferably replaced by:

cs2 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("PC3DataSet-C4", cdf=cdf)

>>bc2 <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs2, tag="BCcoreCDF")
>>csBC2 <- process(bc2,verbose=verbose)
>>setCdf(csBC2,cdf)

I don't this the latter setCdf() is needed here; the CDF should be
carried down automatically.

>>qn2 <- QuantileNormalization(csBC2, typesToUpdate="pm",tags="QNcore")
>>csN2 <- process(qn2)
> Error in list("process(qn2)" = <environment>,
> "process.QuantileNormalization(qn2)" = <environment>, :
>
> [2008-05-20 10:48:38] Exception: Failed to copy file. Temporary copy
> file exists: probeData/PC3DataSet-C4,BCcoreCDF,QNcore/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/
> EGF.CEL.tmp.tmp
> at throw(Exception(...))
> at throw.default("Failed to copy file. Temporary copy file exists:
> ", tmpPathname)
> at throw("Failed to copy file. Temporary copy file exists: ",
> tmpPathname)
> at copyFile.default(getPathname(this), pathname, overwrite =
> overwrite, verbose = less(verbose, 10))
> at copyFile(getPathname(this), pathname, overwrite = overwrite,
> verbose = less(verbose, 10))
> at copyTo.GenericDataFile(this, filename = tmpPathname, path = NULL,
> verbose = less(verbose))
> at copyTo(this, filename = tmpPathname, path = NULL, verbose =
> less(verbose))
> at createFrom.AffymetrixCelFile(this, filename = pathname, path =
> NULL, verbose = less(verbose))
> at createFrom(this, filename = pathname, path = NULL, verbose =
> less(verbose))
> at normalizeQuantile.AffymetrixCelFile(df, path = path,
> subsetToUpdate = subsetToUpdate, t

As Mark said, the error message tells you what is going wrong; there
exists an temporary file 'EGF.CEL.tmp.tmp'. Temporary files are
temporary, so they should be rather safe to delete manually. Try
that. It is there because in a previous session aroma.affymetrix was
interrupted while writing this file.

More over, it is *very* useful to turn on verbose output when
troubleshooting. So, please use

csN2 <- process(qn2, verbose=-10)

to see what the steps are up and until it fails.

As Mark also mentioned, as a last resort you may also want to delete
that directory and directories of downstream analysis completely.

Alternatively, add a tag to your input data set to indicate that you
excluded one file.

>
>
> I also noticed that there is something wrong with the algorith
> patameters/targetDistribution of QuantileNormalisation as i get a
> funny sequence of numbers when i do:
>> print(qn2)
> QuantileNormalization:
> Data set: PC3DataSet-C4
> Input tags: BCcoreCDF
> Output tags: BCcoreCDF,QNcore
> Number of arrays: 10 (627.94MB)
> Chip type: HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core,A20071112,EP
> Algorithm parameters: (subsetToUpdate: NULL, typesToUpdate: chr "pm",
> subsetToAvg: NULL, typesToAvg: chr "pm", .targetDistribution: atomic
> [1:1082385] 2.65 2.70 2.74 2.76 2.77 ..., ..- attr(*, "identifier")=
> chr "0eaa5518c2aece6a8cd6593a19951570")
> Output path: probeData/PC3DataSet-C4,BCcoreCDF,QNcore/HuEx-1_0-st-v2
> Is done: FALSE
> RAM: 8.26MB

If you by "funny sequence of numbers" mean the 'identifier' attribute,
they are extremely useful and makes sure that the target distribution
from your previous and your current run are not mixed up. The
'identifier' is 32-symbol hexadecimal (MD5) code generated from the
input data set used to calculate the target distribution. See the
'digest' package and http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5 for more
details.

Cheers

/Henrik

>
> Can you help???

> Maria
